question.problem:
Use the method of Lagrange multipliers to find the minimum value of the function $f(x,y)={x}^{2}+{y}^{2}\,$ on the parabola ${x}^{2}-2y-4=0.$

*Hint: You may assume that the global minimum of $f(x,y)$ exists on the parabola.*
question.worked_solution:
We must find the minimum value of $f(x,y)$ subject to the constraint $g(x,y)={x}^{2}-2y-4=0.$ Therefore, by the method of Lagrange multipliers, we must solve the following system:

$$
∇f(x,y)=\lambda ∇g(x,y),\,g(x,y)=0
$$

We start by solving the first equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y) & =\lambda ∇g(x,y) \\ ⟨{f}_{x}(x,y),{f}_{y}(x,y)⟩ & =\lambda ⟨{g}_{x}(x,y),{g}_{y}(x,y)⟩ \\ ⟨2x,2y⟩ & =\lambda ⟨2x,-2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}\{\begin{aligned}2x=2\lambda x \\ 2y=-2\lambda \end{aligned}\,⇒\,\{\begin{aligned}x(1-\lambda )=0 \\ y=-\lambda \end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

To solve this system, we break it up into several cases:

- Assuming $x=0$ in the first equation of the system, the constraint condition ${x}^{2}-2y-4=0$ implies

$$
\begin{aligned}-2y-4 & =0\,⇒\,y=-2.\end{aligned}
$$

This gives the critical point $(0,-2).$

- Assuming $\lambda =1$ in the first equation of the system, the second equation of the system implies

$$
\begin{aligned}y=-1.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, the constraint condition ${x}^{2}-2y-4=0$ implies

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+2-4 & =0\,⇒\,x=\pm \sqrt{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

This gives the critical points $(-\sqrt{2},-1),(\sqrt{2},-1).$

Therefore, $f$ has possible extreme values at the points

$$
(0,-2),\,(\pm \sqrt{2},-1).
$$

We evaluate $f$ at these points. These are given in the following table:

| $(x,y)$ | $(0,-2)$ | $(\pm \sqrt{2},-1)$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $f(x,y)$ | $4$ | $3$ |

Therefore, the function reaches a minimum value at the points $(\pm \sqrt{2},-1)$ and its minimum value is $3.$
